- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Forecasts tend to be too high in the first 5–10 days post-spike, then gradually correct — suggesting lagged adjustment to new market conditions.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to anticipate price pullback after peaks, leading to persistent overforecasting.
- When history shows strong downward momentum, model still projects upward bias — especially if recent 7–14 day average is falling.
- Forecasts often overshoot by 3–8% in the first 3–5 days after a spike, then converge — implying model lacks short-term volatility dampening.
- Model underreacts to sustained low prices; when history shows prolonged decline, forecast still holds higher mean, missing bottoming-out.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the 10–20 day horizon — especially when true outcome shows mean reversion or consolidation.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or calendar-driven patterns (e.g., end-of-month or quarter-end price dips).
- When true outcome shows a sharp drop after a peak, model often continues upward trend — suggesting poor lagged response to recent data.
- Model tends to ignore recent low points in history when forecasting — especially if those lows are below 30-day moving average.
